messages:
elaine: Heads-up — ran a full perf profile on 8xA100 after landing fp8 + tp kernel selector change. Seeing ~18% end-to-end latency regression for seq_len=2048 batch=1 (generator workload). nvprof snippets below.

jordan: Can you paste the profiler output and the commit hash?

elaine: commit 7f3a2d9, profiler excerpt: 
```
Step 100: total_step_ms=142.8
- forward_compute_ms=74.1
- backward_compute_ms=0.0 (inference)
- allreduce_ms=28.3  # NCCL AllReduce / AllGather spikes
- memcpy_h2d_ms=9.5
- kernel_launch_overhead_ms=10.2
- idle_wait_ms=20.7
```

sam: interesting — allreduce at 28ms is pretty high for 8xA100. bucket size? lots of small ops?

elaine: default bucket/grad-size heuristics. For inference it's mainly KV cache sync + per-layer rotary/attn matmul reductions. The new fp8 kernels introduce extra host/device syncs in the matmul path (kernel selector falling back for some shapes).

katie: my hunch: kernel selector change caused non-fused matmul path -> extra memcpy + extra stream sync points. Also KV cache sharding currently triggers an all-gather when a rank misses prefix segments. That all-gather is not overlapped.

perf-bot: [regression] perf/runner/master: +17.9% median latency vs baseline (last 7 runs). Suspect: kernel-selector/quant commit 7f3a2d9.

ops-bot: note: kernel-selection policy v2 rolled out in staging at 2027-09-03T19:10Z (rolled to prod 2027-09-04T02:00Z). It enables fp8-kernels for common shapes but falls back to generic GEMM for edge shapes.

jordan: We should try: 1) increase NCCL bucket (reduce op count) 2) force fused fp8 matmul where safe 3) overlap KV all-gather with next-layer compute using CUDA events. Quick pseudo: 
```
// overlap example
recordEvent(eventA, stream_compute);
launch_allgather_async(..., stream_comm);
waitEvent(eventA, stream_comm);
// or better: start comm earlier (after producing KV shards)
```

sam: also check NCCL async progress vs blocking progress mode. On some kernels small ops cause CPU-side stalls. Increasing `NCCL_MIN_NRINGS` and using `ncclCommInitRank` with multithreaded progress helped previous regressions.

elaine: FYI KV cache behavior: with TP sharding we currently map prefix->rank round-robin. If the request accesses prefix spans across ranks we do an explicit all-gather per-layer. That explains the per-layer allreduce spikes. If we instead make per-request local caching (LRU of remote shards) we can avoid repeated all-gathers for conversational traffic.

katie: another angle: fp8 scale instability on TP — quant scales were per-tensor and sometimes underflow for depthwise rows -> dequant noise. Suggest trying per-channel scales or a clamp threshold to reduce numeric noise (fallback to fp16 when scale < epsilon).

jordan: good call. We can run a matrix: { bucket_size: [32MB,64MB,128MB], kernel_mode: [force-fused, selector-default], kv_strategy: [allgather, local-cache], quant_policy: [per-tensor, per-channel, fp16-fallback] } and measure p99/p50 and allreduce time.

elaine: i'll kick off the first two experiments (change bucket, force-fused) and post results. Volunteers to run kv-cache/local-cache prototype? ideally someone familiar with TP shard map.

sam: I can take the kv-cache prototype, will try consistent-hash approach + LRU.

katie: i'll implement per-channel scaling + fp16-fallback toggle in the quant layer and run unit evals for numeric stability on long-context traces.

elaine: thanks — i'll report back with new profiler dumps. TL;DR: likely root cause = selector fallback + small NCCL op count + un-overlapped per-layer all-gather from KV sharding + fp8 scale edge cases.

perf-bot: tagging SLA-alert if p99 > 2s after next run. :eyes:

ops-bot: remember to add feature flag for force-fused and kv-local-cache so we can roll back fast.

elaine: noted. I'll set flags and schedule A/B runs tomorrow morning.
